acceptance: The hosted Agent's chats are tabs of the native workbench opened from the launcher; opening one sends nothing, each keeps its own composer and draft, and moving a chat into a split keeps the same content instance without reading runs again. A second conversation may run while another is active, and closing a tab never stops its run. History is read once per Agent for concurrent refreshes, never preloads transcripts, refuses a conversation another tab shows, and opening one restores only its runs. A tab holding an unconfirmed submission cannot be closed until it is confirmed, while other tabs stay usable; after a restart a pending submission is confirmed by its original receipt and never submitted twice.

What a hosted chat holds (its draft and pending submission) belongs to its workspace identity — API, account, Project and root: another account, API or Project starts empty and the same identity finds it again. Showing a local project closes the hosted Agent's location and the hosted Project brings its own workbench back. A late receipt lands on the chat that sent it, never on the next Project's.

reason: TS keys a hosted chat's in-memory draft by the session generation too, so the same account signing in again sees an empty composer until it returns to the old generation. The native app keeps a hosted chat's draft and pending submission in its persisted identity (API, account, Project, root), so they survive the same account signing in again; this is what lets a pending receipt be confirmed after a re-sign-in, and another account never sees them.

acceptance: Header Sign in and the place menu's Sign in open the same explainer without starting browser sign-in until it is confirmed; its two Cloud moments auto-advance, loop, pause on hover and switch on a dot; Escape or Close dismisses it without starting sign-in; a browser sign-in failure is shown in the dialog with retry; completing sign-in closes it.

Publishing a folder is one task in the window's own dialog layer with no services navigation or provider switch; Escape (or Close) puts the dialog away without cancelling the publication, which completes in the background and the Header states the run; signed out, the same dialog asks to sign in and Escape closes it.

A publication asks which organization unless there is only one, remembering no earlier choice (so nothing carries over to another Cloud host); a destination chosen before the page opened is kept only if the account may still create projects there and is never swapped for another; a list read for an earlier checkout or account is dropped.
